Your caster

🃏 Spell cards

Poker-size cards (2.5 × 3.5 in, 63 × 88 mm), nine to a page with dashed lines to cut along. Print at 100% scale (not "fit to page"). Tick Backs too and print on both sides (flip on the long edge) for a patterned back on every card. Attack, feature, and magic item cards are on 🎴 Feature & Item Cards.

Pick a Character Builder character and your picks and favorites save onto it, in this browser. A caster of your own lives in the address bar, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it and a reload keeps it; nothing else is saved.
The spellcasting rules and spell lists are from the System Reference Document 5.1 by Wizards of the Coast LLC, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. The one-line spell summaries are the Gazette's own; each card links to the spell's full text.

How preparing spells works in 5e

Clerics, druids, paladins, and wizards don't learn a fixed set of spells. Each day they pick, or prepare, a list from the spells they could cast, and that list is what they can cast until they change it. Bards, rangers, sorcerers, and warlocks know their spells instead: the list only changes when they gain a level.

How many spells you can prepare

ClassPrepared spellsPrepares from
✨ ClericWisdom modifier + cleric levelthe whole cleric spell list
🌿 DruidWisdom modifier + druid levelthe whole druid spell list
🛡️ PaladinCharisma modifier + half the paladin level, rounded downthe whole paladin spell list (from level 2)
📜 WizardIntelligence modifier + wizard levelthe spells in your spellbook

The total is always at least 1, and every spell must be of a level you have slots for. A 5th-level cleric with 16 Wisdom prepares 3 + 5 = 8 spells of 1st to 3rd level. Domain spells for a cleric, oath spells for a paladin, and circle spells for a Circle of the Land druid are always prepared and don't count against the total. Cantrips aren't prepared at all: you always know them.

Changing them after a long rest

When you finish a long rest you can change your prepared list. It takes a minute of prayer, meditation, or study per spell level for each spell you prepare, so a list of eight spells averaging 2nd level takes about a quarter of an hour. Preparing a spell doesn't use a slot; casting it does, and you can cast a prepared spell from any slot of its level or higher.

Using the planner

  • 🌙 Long Rest: Change Prepared Spells opens the picker; the count stops you at your limit, and the line under the filter shows what's going out and coming in. ✓ Done keeps the list, ✕ Cancel puts the old one back.
  • ☆ Favorites are the spells you prepare most. Star them anywhere, then ⭐ Start from Favorites fills the list with them and leaves the rest to pick.
  • Wizards fill the spellbook first (📜 Edit Spellbook), then prepare from it. Known casters use ✏️ Change Spells Known when they level up.
  • Spell cards show the casting time, range, components, duration, and a one-line summary, plus the address of the full spell text. Print today's list, your favorites, a wizard's whole spellbook, or every spell your class can cast.

Works with

Build the character in the Character Builder and pick it here; its scores and level set the limits. The Spellbook searches all 319 SRD spells by level, school, class, concentration, and ritual, and the Multiclass Calculator works out the slots when a caster takes a second class.
